title: Gengo: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Tōkaidō Stamp Book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Tōkaidō Stamp Book
options.lineage: Japanese eki stamp books and Edo travel passes, with Hiroshige's prints
options.thesis: Your study is a walk along the Tōkaidō: each station you reach gets a vermilion stamp in your travel book, beside its Hiroshige print.
options.viewport: Top: the current station's print, with its title in a cartouche. Middle: one vermilion stamp-shaped button, '23 due'. Bottom: three small seals along the road for the three of you. Bars, sheets and buttons follow each phone's OS.
options.risk: Ukiyo-e can tip into souvenir-shop kitsch if the prints get scroll frames and fake brush fonts around them.

raised.raise: State shows in how the stamp is printed, not in extra colours: a crisp impression is mastered, a faint one is fading, a half one is learning.
The group board reorders rows in place, and a row that changed stays vermilion until you've seen it.
During a session, only the next decision is on screen, with the kana at monumental size.
The kana is the interface: huge, with no chrome around it.

options.label: Living Hiroshige Plate
options.thesis: The current station's print is the whole background, and the UI sits on it as the print's own title cartouches and seal labels.
options.viewport: The print fills the screen. A vertical cartouche at the top right names the station; the due count is a red seal near the bottom.
options.risk: It's the obvious reading of the brief, and text over a busy print fights for legibility on small phones.

options.label: Boarding Pass and Gate Board
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and departure boards
options.thesis: Today's session is a boarding pass, and the group is a live departure board that reorders as people study.
options.viewport: A pass for today's session (due, new, streak in labelled segments) above the board of the three of you.
options.case: Fits the journey and the shared board well, but it's an airport, not the Tōkaidō, so it fights the pinned prints.
options.risk: Generic travel-app look, with no link to Japanese.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: State shown as line form on one rail.
options.viewport: One rail with every item a tick on it.
options.risk: Cold and scientific, the opposite of a warm journey.
options.case: Loses on both: learners don't see themselves in a lab plate.
options.kept: State carried by form (how the stamp is printed) instead of extra colours.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: One next decision, signed at monumental scale.
options.viewport: A yellow band naming the next thing to do.
options.risk: Shouty, and it ignores the prints.
options.case: Loses on both: an airport, not Japan, and not the journey.
options.kept: Only the next decision on screen, at monumental scale.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.risk: Dated, and it fights both OS conventions.
options.case: Loses on both: it conflicts with the native-per-OS decision.
options.kept: The kana is the interface: huge, chrome deleted.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.viewport: A night chart of your kana.
options.risk: A second metaphor competing with the journey.
options.case: Loses on both: the brief already pins the Tōkaidō journey.
options.kept: Nothing new; the stamp's impression already ranks strength.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean language-app look like Duolingo or Renshuu, done well.
canonCard.viewport: A greeting, a progress ring and a big green Continue button, with the prints on a separate tab.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other study app, which is the clutter Chris left.
